newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on CBOT, wheat down limit.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on CBOT, wheat down limit.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended down on a downward reversal in Chicago's soycomplex and commercial selling.

"The reversal in the beans really weighed on us. Cargill was a big seller, the Pools were good buyers and exporters bought the March," a trader said. Nov-Jan spread at $2, Jan May at $2.80, May-July $3. Volume was 5,950 lots, 200 hedges.
Mexico bought 30,000 tonnes of canola for March delivery, Japan bought 15,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
November canola fell $2.30 to $434.90, January lost $1.40 to $437.10. October flax rose $0.40 to $407.60 a tonne to set a new high with XCan and Cargill buying, traders said. Volume was 400 lots.

Feed wheat ended limit down on ideas snow will downgrade significant amounts of wheat to feed quality. Dec-Mar spread at $7.50, Oct-Dec at $15. Volume was 1,950 lots. Limits were expanded to $7.50 for the next three sessions.
November western barley lost $3.80 to $145.70 as Midland Walwyn sold 500 against feedlot buying. July-Oct spread at $1, March-May at $2.50. Volume was 2,800 lots.
Cargill bought 25 December oats up the US$5 limit to US$131.20, traders said.
Cargill also bought December peas down US$0.50 at US$205.50 a tonne, they said.. Volume was 120 lots.
(All values in Canadian dollars except peas, oats)
